title: 专家应对疫苗犹豫：个性化对话，比统一宣传更有效？
speaker: Dr. Amish Adolgez

segments.en: So I think it depends upon why someone is not vaccinated. There may be people who haven't gotten around to getting their children vaccinated.
segments.zh: 我认为这取决于人们未接种的原因，有些人可能只是还没带孩子去接种。

segments.en: There may be people who have questions about vaccines. So you kind of have to take a different tack depending upon where someone is.
segments.zh: 有些人可能对疫苗有疑问，需要根据具体情况采取不同策略。

segments.en: And often it's very different to do it kind of as a one-size-fits-all message on television by a talking head versus a provider sitting in front of a patient or a patient's family.
segments.zh: 电视上统一宣传与医生面对患者进行个性化沟通效果截然不同。

segments.en: And I think that's the better way to do it. We know that people will move towards vaccination if they can get their answers to the questions that they have in a non-judgmental way.
segments.zh: 这是更好的方式，如果人们能在非评判的环境中解答疑问，他们更可能选择接种。

segments.en: That's a very different type of rhetoric when you're dealing with the likes of RFK Jr. who is spreading disinformation where you just have to basically call him out for spreading lies.
segments.zh: 这与应对RFK Jr.等散布虚假信息的人截然不同，对后者需要直接揭穿谎言。

segments.en: So it's very kind of nuanced and very personalized. And that's what works. We know that parents trust family doctors, they trust their primary care providers.
segments.zh: 因此需要细致且个性化的方法，这很有效。我们知道家长信任家庭医生和初级保健提供者。

segments.en: That's where the actual movement occurs, not so much when someone's on blasting from a megaphone about the vaccine.
segments.zh: 真正的改变发生在那里，而不是通过大喇叭喊话。
